punchline: One study found people at 29, 39 or 49 were 48 percent overrepresented among first-time marathon runners, a finding later disputed.
thirty_sec: Adam Alter and Hal Hershfield found that '9-enders' are far more likely to run their first marathon, as if a new decade triggers a life audit. Daniel Pink links that to midpoints: student teams switched strategies around day six of an eleven-day project, and NBA teams down by one at halftime won more often than expected.
